summary: Scheduled report annotations become non-sequential for EU timezones during clock fallback hour
description:
Issue summary:
Customers in EU (CET/CEST) report that scheduled PDF/dashboard snapshots include metric annotations with timestamps that are out of order (non-monotonic) when the scheduler runs during the clock fallback hour (end of DST).

Impact:
- Nimbus Apps (enterprise) reported 4 scheduled reports (daily summary) produced on 2026-03-11 showing annotation timestamps that jump backwards within the same timeseries, causing confusion for auditors.
- Affects scheduled exports and PDF snapshots only (console manual export appears correct).
- Frequency: reproducible when job runs between 01:00 and 02:10 local time on fallback day.

Environment:
- prod-eu-west (report-scheduler service in eu-west-1)
- Customer org: Nimbus Apps, several dashboards with annotation rules and alert markers

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Customer has a daily scheduled snapshot set to 01:30 Europe/Paris timezone (recurring).
2) On DST fallback (clocks go from 03:00 -> 02:00 local), scheduler triggered the job during the duplicated hour.
3) Generated PDF shows annotations with timestamps: 02:42, 02:49, 02:11, 02:55 (non-sequential).

Expected behavior:
- Annotation timestamps should be ordered ascending in the exported report, matching the underlying timeseries ordering in the console.

Actual behavior:
- Timestamps are ordered according to a mapping that seems to mix server UTC epoch with ambiguous local times, producing out-of-order annotation rows in the final document.

Logs / artifacts attached:
- scheduler-log-snippet-2026-03-11.txt (contains two schedule events with same local hour but different UTC epochs)
- screenshot-annotated-report-2026-03-11.png (highlighted annotation order in PDF)

Notes on customer impact and urgency:
- Enterprise customer (Nimbus Apps) has internal compliance reviews tied to daily reports; incorrect ordering is causing manual reconciliation work. Customer requested ETA for fix and a short-term mitigation.

2026-03-12 13:42 - Engineering (Elena Ruiz): Initial hypothesis: report-snapshot generator sorts annotations by naive-localtime string after conversion instead of epoch; ambiguous DST 'fold' is not handled when converting event_time -> localtime. Adding to backlog for fix; will prototype patch to use zoneinfo with fold awareness.

2026-03-13 08:30 - Support (Sofia Patel): Shared customer workaround: change schedule to 03:15 local (post-fallback) or 00:30 (pre-overlap) to avoid duplicated hour until patch is deployed. Customer accepted temporary schedule change.

2026-03-14 11:00 - Engineering (Liam O'Connor): Small patch prepared: https://github.com/redwood/reports/pull/2315 — updates annotation timestamp sort key to use integer epoch_ms and preserves original timezone-aware datetime for display. Running integration tests against fallback day fixtures.

2026-03-14 15:26 - Support (Sofia Patel): Informed customer about patch and suggested rollback plan for production rollout. Customer asked for ETA for production deploy and whether historical reports need re-generation.
investigation_notes: Reproduced with unit test that creates two events: 2026-10-31 02:15+01:00 (fold=1) and 2026-10-31 02:05+02:00 (fold=0) — naive string sort yields 02:05,02:15 then incorrectly maps when identical local time strings are used downstream.

Root cause: report-renderer pipeline converts event timestamps to localized string labels early and later sorts by that label when building annotation table. During DST fallback, labels are ambiguous (same HH:MM) and lose epoch ordering.

Scheduler emits two jobs with distinct UTC epochs but the downstream PDF generator uses the formatted label as stable sort key — should use epoch_ms as primary key and fall back to label for display only.
Potential ripple: any feature that builds 'annotation tables' from pre-formatted times could exhibit similar issues in other regions with DST transitions.
Test plan: add fixture for ambiguous hour in unit/integration tests, run nightly job simulator, and add e2e snapshot validation comparing console vs PDF export ordering.
Mitigation plan: instruct affected customers to reschedule daily snapshot outside overlap hours; backend hotfix to be staged tomorrow (2026-03-15) then rolled to prod with feature flag.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood/reports/pull/2315 — includes changelog entry and migration notes for report renderer.
recommended_workaround: Temporarily reschedule daily snapshots to run outside the DST overlap window (e.g., 03:30 local after fallback or 00:30 before overlap) or use manual export from console until fix is deployed.
next_steps: 1) Complete code review and CI for PR #2315. 2) Deploy to staging and run DST overlap simulation harness. 3) Coordinate small production rollout behind feature flag, monitor a sample of customer scheduled reports for the next fallback window. 4) Communicate ETA and deployment windows to Nimbus Apps before production rollout.
